claims.text: explicit symbolic reasoning integrated into scaled deep learning models is essential to overcome limitations associated with non-differentiable phase boundaries in deep learning

post-hoc methods like distillation and gradient approximation can sufficiently bridge the gap for non-differentiable phase boundaries in scaled deep learning models without explicit symbolic reasoning
explicit symbolic reasoning integrated into scaled deep learning models is necessary to overcome limitations of non-differentiable phase boundaries in out-of-distribution generalization

post-hoc methods like distillation and gradient approximation are insufficient to bridge the gap for non-differentiable phase boundaries in scaled deep learning models under out-of-distribution generalization

post-hoc methods like distillation and gradient approximation are insufficient to bridge the gap for non-differentiable phase boundaries in scaled deep learning models without explicit symbolic reasoning

explicit symbolic reasoning integrated into scaled deep learning models is necessary to overcome limitations of non-differentiable phase boundaries in out-of-distribution generalization, but only when the phase boundaries are induced by compositional rule changes rather than continuous feature shifts
implicit learning mechanisms can overcome limitations of non-differentiable phase boundaries in out-of-distribution generalization

explicit symbolic reasoning integrated into scaled deep learning models is sufficient to eliminate the performance gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization on tasks with non-differentiable phase boundaries
scaled deep learning models can overcome limitations of non-differentiable phase boundaries in out-of-distribution generalization without explicit symbolic reasoning
